092: 1382–1450. A low EMPTY stall interior is the whole foreground: bare pegs, rolled mat and abandoned pottery shelf. In central daylight doorway framed by these abandoned goods stands one full-length tax collector FACING THE VIEWER, looking uncomfortable and holding a heavy bulging leather money bag low down. Behind him only two distant open stalls in otherwise empty market. No foreground observer's back, no pair, no cathedral. Spring grey daylight. Visual irony: much collected money but almost nobody trading. Clear broad quiet shapes rather than a document scene.
096: 1382–1450. A wooden loom with its broken crossbeam occupies THREE QUARTERS of picture, close side-on mechanical view in barn interior open to late summer orchard. Only one borrower, a young woman with covered hair, crouches below the loom to align the visibly freshly broken pale crossbeam fragment with a darker old worn joint. Full small figure, no facing people across work surface. Old polished peg and new bright splintered wood are both large enough to contrast. Warp threads hang slack diagonally down left, wooden shuttle on floor. The action is inspecting damage to a borrowed loom at season's end, not weaving.
097: 1382–1450. Bird's eye view from almost directly above a small river cargo boat under way towards medieval London Bridge visible only as a thin upper horizon landmark. Boat long axis diagonal bottom left to top right dominates with two bales, coils of rope and one folded BLANK parchment packet with plain red wax seal tied atop cargo. TWO merchants seated near boat bow FACE UP TOWARD CAMERA, one extends an empty leather purse toward the other as distant London credit is discussed; a boatman at stern rows. They are SMALL full figures embedded in boat geometry, not foreground back observers watching a harbour. Misty autumn dawn, river fills nearly all background, bridge roofline has NO chimneys. Warm muted painterly brushwork, no text on packet.
